visual.general_description: Grayscale brain magnetic resonance venography composite of two side-by-side head projections; the left image carries one white arrow and the right image carries no annotation.
visual.detailed_description: One low-resolution grayscale image holds two side-by-side images separated by a thin dark vertical line. Both show a head outline filled with bright branching tubular structures on a dark background. In the left image a bright vertical tubular structure near the midline runs from near the top to the lower middle part, with finer bright vessels arching to both sides. Near the lower part of the left image there are bright curved horizontal tubular structures: a large one extends to the right from just below the lower end of the vertical structure, a smaller one lies beneath it on the right, and a third lies at the lower left; tubular structures descend below them at lower left and lower right. One solid white arrow sits in the lower central part of the left image, with its head at the left end pointing at the right edge of the lower part of the vertical structure; its shaft rises slightly toward the right. The right image shows an oval head outline with a gray soft-tissue halo, a vertical bright tubular structure near the midline from the upper middle to the bottom, arching vessels on both sides, bright curved tubular structures in the lower half (including a large C-shaped one on the right side of the image that ends in a brighter irregular area near its upper end and meets a bright confluence at the bottom center) and a smaller bright curved vessel at the left. The right image has no arrow or other annotation. No panel letters, titles, patient text, timestamps, device text or scale bars are visible in either image.

pixel_observations: Grayscale image, 716 by 443 pixels, with two side-by-side images separated by a thin dark vertical line; no panel letters, titles, scale bars, patient text, timestamps or device text are visible.
Left image: head outline with a bright vertical tubular structure near the midline running from near the top to the lower middle part and finer bright vessels arching and branching to both sides.

Left image: bright curved horizontal tubular structures in the lower part (a large one extending to the right from just below the lower end of the vertical structure, a smaller one beneath it on the right, and one at the lower left) with tubular structures descending below them at lower left and lower right.
Left image: one solid white arrow in the lower central part, head at its left end pointing at the right edge of the lower part of the vertical structure, shaft rising slightly toward the right.
Right image: oval head outline with a gray soft-tissue halo, a vertical bright tubular structure near the midline from the upper middle to the bottom and arching vessels on both sides.

Right image: bright curved tubular structures in the lower half, including a large C-shaped one on the right side of the image ending in a brighter irregular area near its upper end, a smaller bright curved vessel at the left and a bright confluence at the bottom center; no arrow or other annotation.

caption_claims.value: The caption states only that the figure shows brain magnetic resonance venography; it names no patient, view, side or arrow.

clinical_significance.statement: The Methods cite Figure 1 where they say CVT was diagnosed from the clinical signs and confirmed by neuroimaging findings by magnetic resonance venography; the caption states no finding and the text does not explain the arrow.

evidence.quote: CVT was diagnosed based on the clinical signs and confirmed by neuroimaging findings by magnetic resonance venography (Figure 1)

limitations: Low-resolution grayscale composite: fine vessels cannot be characterized and no signal change along any vessel can be reliably described.
The caption and text do not explain the white arrow, name any vessel, side or view, or say whether the two images are two views of one patient or images of two patients.
No panel letters are printed, so the whole figure is one panel; the two images are described separately in the detailed description and pixel observations.
No vessel is named in the pixel observations because the image carries no labels; any anatomical naming would come from the authors, not from the image.
Pixels were viewed at full resolution with enlarged crops of both images, the arrow region, the image edges and a brightened copy; no hidden text or labels were found.
